title: 2005 AMC 12B Problem 24
statement: All three vertices of an equilateral triangle are on the parabola \(y = x^2,\) and one of its sides has a slope of \(2.\) The \(x\)-coordinates of the three vertices have a sum of \(\dfrac{m}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is the value of \(m + n?\)

solutions.text:
For vertices \((a, a^2), (b, b^2), (c, c^2),\) the slope of a side is \(\dfrac{b^2 - a^2}{b - a} = a + b.\) Adding the three side slopes, \[ \begin{aligned} &(a+b) + (b+c) + (c+a) \\ &= 2(a + b + c) \\ &= 2 \cdot \dfrac{m}{n}. \end{aligned} \]

One side has slope \(2 = \tan\theta.\) Because the triangle is equilateral, its sides make angles \(\theta\) and \(\theta \pm 60^\circ,\) so the other two slopes are \[ \begin{aligned} &\tan(\theta \pm 60^\circ) = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt3}{1 \mp 2\sqrt3} \\ &= -\dfrac{8 \pm 5\sqrt3}{11}. \end{aligned} \]

The sum of the three slopes is \(2 - \dfrac{8 + 5\sqrt3}{11}\) \(- \dfrac{8 - 5\sqrt3}{11} =\) \(\dfrac{22 - 16}{11} = \dfrac{6}{11}.\)

Thus \(a + b + c = \dfrac12 \cdot \dfrac{6}{11} = \dfrac{3}{11},\) so \(m + n = 3 + 11 = 14.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The chord joining \((a, a^2)\) and \((b, b^2)\) has slope \(a + b\)
The three side slopes are \(\tan\theta\) and \(\tan(\theta \pm 60^\circ)\); their sum is twice the vertex-sum
